name: Father Mathew Bridge
facts: Father Mathew Bridge, originally Dublin Bridge, first appeared in 1014 as a wooden ford, evolving through Norman, medieval, and Victorian reconstructions before its 1818 stone incarnation.
The 1818 stone bridge, designed by George Knowles, replaced the collapsed 14th‑century masonry bridge and was later renamed in 1938 after temperance advocate Father Theobald Mathew.
For 390 years, the original four‑arch bridge hosted shops, a chapel, and even a house built by Mayor Geoffrey de Morton, a rare example of commercial life on a Dublin bridge.
